What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of an ellipse with equation 
$\frac{{x}^{2}}{50}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{98}=1?$
question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

In the given equation, we have ${a}^{2}=50$ and ${b}^{2}=98.$

- Since ${a}^{2}=50,$ the length of the horizontal radius must be $a=\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}.$

- Since ${b}^{2}=98,$ the length of the vertical radius must be $b=\sqrt{98}=7\sqrt{2}.$

So the semi-major axis has length $b=7\sqrt{2},$ and the semi-minor axis has length $a=5\sqrt{2}.$

Therefore, the major axis has length $2b=2\cdot 7\sqrt{2}=14\sqrt{2},$ and the minor axis has length $2a=2\cdot 5\sqrt{2}=10\sqrt{2}.$
